lessons: Framed the skill around one guiding principle ('the browser is the attacker's tool') and ten commandments, each mapped to a concrete Israeli disclosure or an OWASP category, so findings are grounded rather than opinion.

Scanner discipline: scripts/scan.sh emits leads, not findings. The instructions force a read-in-context step (innerHTML on a constant string is not a finding; findById(id) after an ownership check is not a finding) so the agent does not report false positives from grep output.

Anti-injection hardening of the scanner itself: a repository being scanned must not be able to execute code through the scanner. CI asserts this with a crafted filename ('--pre=sh') that ripgrep would otherwise parse as a command-executing flag; the test fails if a PWNED marker appears.

Dual-engine self-check: scan.sh runs under ripgrep and grep -E, which accept different regex dialects. An early pattern was rejected by ripgrep only while 2>/dev/null hid the error, making a whole category look clean. Rejected patterns now print PATTERN FAILED and the script exits 2.

deferred: scan.sh is grep, not AST: it misses obfuscated code and cross-file flows. The read-in-context step is mandatory precisely because of this ceiling.

lessons: Reach fix: SKILL.md is now English-primary with a full Hebrew companion (SKILL_HE.md), and reports still adapt to the user's language. Added adapters/security-rules.md so the ruleset works in Cursor, Windsurf, Copilot, Codex/OpenCode and Gemini CLI, not only Claude.

Claude Desktop compatibility fix: the enriched metadata (display_name, display_description, tags, supported_agents) was living in the SKILL.md frontmatter, which Claude Desktop rejects. Moved it all to a separate metadata.json and reduced the frontmatter to name, description and license.

Added a real-world case to references/commandments.md: the July 2026 Guardio / Adobe Acrobat Chrome-extension WhatsApp-takeover chain (unauthenticated internal message channel + test-only code shipped to production), which illustrates commandments 2 and 6 with a fresh, verifiable Israeli-research disclosure.

Infra to Skills IL standard: added metadata.json, evidence.json (claims grounded in the Elector, Beit Shemesh and cannabis-site disclosures, the Guardio case, OWASP, and the 2017 Data Security Regulations) and this optimization-log.json. Enabled secret scanning, CodeQL, and a Sigstore-attested signed release; restricted the test workflow's GITHUB_TOKEN to contents:read.
Style: removed em dashes and en dashes across the skill files per the Skills IL project rule, replacing them with ASCII hyphens, commas or parentheses.

deferred: The skill is mirrored at the repo root (for the submission form) and in skills/ran-bar-zik/ (for install). The two copies must be kept in sync manually; a CI drift-check is a candidate for a future cycle.
references/ still contain Hebrew-first detail; an English pass on the references would widen reach further but is not required for the review flow, which is driven by SKILL.md.

lessons: New capability, not just new prose: scan.sh only ever read the text of code, so 'who is allowed to read this repo' was a total blind spot. Section 0 asks git instead of grep (visibility via gh, plus .env / key / csv / sqlite files tracked in the index), which is exactly the vector behind the August 2026 IDF infantry-school case.

A red-flag filter that cries wolf stops being read: the first version of section 0 matched every path containing 'secret' and flagged an .env.example and a key-rotation doc. Narrowed it to real data and credential files.
Commandment 9 now covers the agent itself and not only its output: the agent pushes projects to public repos, and 'Make it secure' in a prompt is an instruction, not a control.
Commandment 10 now treats a quiet fix as no fix: a report with no owner, ticket and due date is not handled, and the product needs a documented reporting channel.
Stated the ceiling instead of implying coverage: without gh, section 0 reports 'visibility unknown' and a public repo holding only source is still missed. Documented in both READMEs.

Follow-up case, same affair (31 Aug 2026): told to 'add security', the agent built a login form that kept its result as loggedIn:true in sessionStorage. Section 1 of the scanner would not have caught it, so the pattern now covers session/localStorage auth flags, and test_scan.sh asserts that alternative on a fixture of its own rather than on the shared vulnerable file, where it could have rotted unnoticed.

Commandment 10 now says 'reported fixed' is not 'verified fixed': the same system was declared closed and a week later exposed both the old data and 996 new civilian records. Re-attack the same path after the fix, and escalate to the regulator when the owner does not close it.
A fix produced by an agent is new code, not a patch: it gets a full review, including whatever it published while fixing.

Release red-team on our own scanner: section 0 prints git remotes, and a remote URL can carry a token (https://user:token@host/...), so the scanner would have echoed a live credential into a CI log. Credentials are stripped before printing, with a fixture whose remote carries a token asserting it never appears in the output.

Supply chain, applied to ourselves: the release attested SKILL.md, SKILL_HE.md and metadata.json while scan.sh, the one file users actually execute, shipped unsigned. The attestation now covers scripts, references and the adapter.

The manual mirror sync deferred in 1.1.0 is now enforced in CI: a diff step fails the build when the root copy and skills/ran-bar-zik/ disagree, so two different skills can never be published under one tag.

deferred: Section 0 cannot determine repository visibility without the gh CLI. A git-remote-only heuristic (for example querying the forge API unauthenticated) is a candidate for a future cycle.
The root mirror and skills/ran-bar-zik/ copies are still synced by hand, and this cycle had to touch eight mirrored files. The CI drift-check deferred in 1.1.0 is now overdue.
